headline: Committee discussed a Latin American cultural festivals resolution and the Burlington Forward public safety resolution without voting on either.
summary: The committee heard public comment and staff updates, then discussed a draft resolution recognizing Burlington's Latin American community and cultural festivals, and reviewed the Burlington Forward resolution on public safety using Vermont's Equity Impact Assessment framework. No votes were taken on either resolution; the committee plans to return recommendations to City Council by September 14th after two additional special meetings on August 25th and September 1st.

• Call to Order 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson called the meeting to order at 5:33 pm on August 18th. 
• Agenda and Meeting Minutes 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson motioned to adopt the agenda and minutes. The motion passed 
unanimously. 
• Public Forum 
o Brian Cliffords spoke in opposition to police-related measures included in the Burlington Forward 
resolution. He offered his technical and data analysis experience to assist the City in reviewing policing 
data and understanding racial disparities. Refer to the video. 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson thanked him for bringing the information forward and noted that 
the committee is considering a dedicated meeting focused on use-of-force and enforcement. 
o Dave Rappaport expressed his concerns regarding the policing data and the need for a sustained effort 
rather than a single meeting to address racial disparities in policing. He offered his time and expertise to 
assist with future work. He also offered to connect the committee with members of White Men for 
Racial Justice who might be interested in participating. Refer to the video. 
o Sarah Russell spoke about the housing and homelessness components of the Burlington Forward 
resolution. She raised concerns that the resolution may imply that alternatives to unsheltered 
homelessness are readily available when there is currently a significant shortage of shelter and housing 
resources. She expressed concern that policies involving more forceful enforcement approaches could 
disproportionately affect BIPOC residents experiencing homelessness. Refer to the video. 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson thanked Sarah Russell for providing this context and noted the 
importance of using current data and community information when developing solutions. 
• Office of REIB Updates 
o Director Kelli Perkins shared updates regarding the REIB’s ongoing work. REIB will bring 
recommendations for Aging Council appointees to the upcoming City Council meeting. She noted that 
recruiting volunteers for city committees and initiatives has been challenging and that some community 
members have expressed hesitancy about participating because of their feelings about the current 
administration and the City’s work. REIB plans to conduct focus groups with Burlington residents who 
are older adults to gather feedback on where the City should begin implementing priority measures 
identified in the 2024 Age Strong Burlington report. Christian Berry continues to work on updating the 
City’s Language Access Plan. REIB is identifying vital City documents that should be translated materials 
themselves. Staff are working toward a broader implementation plan for language access and plan to 
bring department leaders together for training and coordination. Director Perkins reported that the City 
employee culture survey received approximately a 30% response rate. REIB is completing department-
level analysis and expects to provide the committee with a report-out at a future meeting. Director 
Perkins noted that the survey results can help REIB advise departments on creating a more equitable 
workplace where employees feel a sense of belonging and see opportunities for professional growth. 
REIB also reported that 168 backpacks had been collected for a school supply drive serving Burlington 
School District students. Refer to the video. 
• Draft Resolution: Recognizing the Contributions of Burlington’s Latin American Community and Supporting 
Cultural Festivals- Draft Resolution 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson introduced a draft resolution recognizing the contributions of Burlington’s 
Latin American community and supporting cultural festivals. The resolution recognizes the importance 
of cultural celebrations and calls for development of a longer-term, sustainable strategy for cultural 
festivals in partnership with REIB, Burlington City Arts, and community organizations. 
▪ Councilor Grant expressed strong support of the Latin American Festival after attending the 
previous year. She emphasized that cultural events create positive activity in downtown
Burlington, bring families into public spaces, and help residents recognize and celebrate the 
contributions of different communities. 
o Director Perkins explained that REIB provided approximately $5,000 to the Latin American Festival 
during each of the previous two fiscal years. She noted that REIB’s Community Celebrations funding line 
has significant demand and that the office is using a rubric to evaluate requests as it works to distribute 
limited resources. 
▪ Councilor Grant encouraged funding requests be forwarded to City Councilors as additional 
funding may be available through the City Council initiative funds to support requests. 
o Christine Hughes of the Richard Kemp Center described the organization’s work as a cultural 
empowerment center focused on the experiences, history, and contributions of Black Americans. She 
discussed the Center’s block parties, cultural empowerment summit, urban garden programming, and 
annual community trip to Washington, D.C. Christine Hughes shared that the Center experienced 
negative pushback regarding its block party this tear and characterized the response as racist.  
▪ Councilor Grant noted that the Department of Public Works has generally been supportive of 
block parties and requested additional advance notice for future events to allow for appropriate 
planning and traffic management. She discussed facilitating a meeting between the relevant 
parties to address concerns directly and avoid miscommunication between community 
organizations and City departments. 
o Rev. Mark Hughes discussed African Landing Day as a cultural empowerment activity and flagship 
initiative of the Vermont Racial Justice Alliance. He expressed interest in developing a more 
institutionalized relationship between the City and recurring cultural celebrations. He encouraged the 
committee to devote future meetings to the REIB Department’s internal citywide work, including 
training and education, data collection, policy, HR functions, and strategic oversight 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson agreed that institutionalizing support for cultural celebrations 
could help make the work sustainable rather than relying on individual organizations or one-
time funding. She also noted that the City’s employee culture survey could provide an 
opportunity to begin a broader conversation about REIB’s internal and citywide work. 
o Committee members discussed the need for organizations to submit funding requests as early as 
possible because of limited City resources and the multiple steps required for Council initiative funding. 
▪ Requests may require review by Councilors, preparation of supporting materials, Board of 
Finance consideration, and City Council approval. The committee encouraged organizations to 
seek multiple funding sources and to communicate funding needs early. 
• Equity Impact Assessment: Burlington Forward: A Comprehensive Framework For Safe Public Spaces And A 
Stronger Community 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson introduced the committee’s discussion of the Burlington Forward 
resolution concerning public safety in public spaces. The resolution was introduced on August 3rd and 
referred to four City Council committees, including REIB. The committee is expected to provide 
recommendations to City Council, with September 14th identified as the anticipated date for returning 
recommendations. 
▪ Two additional special REIB meetings were scheduled for August 25th and September 1st to 
continue the discussion. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson introduced Vermont’s Equity Impact Assessment as a potential framework 
for evaluating the resolution. She noted that Burlington doesn’t currently have a formal equity 
assessment tool for policies and resolutions. 
o Dylan Pilcher asked about the legal authority of City Council resolutions and whether the Mayor would 
be legally required to implement the recommendations contained in Burlington Forward.  
▪ Councilor Grant explained that City Council resolutions can sometimes express priorities without 
creating legally binding requirements.
▪ Councilor Carpenter explained that Burlington operates under a strong mayoral system and that 
resolutions generally function as recommendations rather than binding directives to the Mayor. 
She characterized Burlington Forward as a starting point for a larger conversation rather than a 
finished product. She emphasized the importance of obtaining additional input from 
departments, community members service providers, and other stakeholders before finalizing 
recommendations. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson noted that the City Attorney has already reviewed the resolution and 
identified areas that would need to be addressed. She stated that legal review would continue as the 
committee develops recommendations. 
o Sarah Russell raised concerns that the resolution did not appear to be receiving discussion from other 
committees in the way she expected and emphasized the importance of transparent public 
engagement. She supported the use of an Equity Impact Assessment and emphasized the need to 
consider the combined impacts of policing disparities and the disproportionate representation of BIPOC 
residents among people experiencing homelessness. 
o The committee discussed the need for a more equitable process for developing future resolutions and 
policies. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson identified several potential elements for a future City policy-development 
framework: 
▪ Legal review and feasibility 
▪ Use of current and appropriate language 
▪ Inclusion of people directly affected by proposed policies. 
▪ Engagement with service providers and other people working directly in the affected areas 
▪ Consideration of research and evidence 
▪ Evaluation of health and social impacts 
o Director Perkins emphasized that policy development should begin by clearly identifying and defining 
the problem. Refer to the video 
o Christian Berry emphasized the importance of centering people who are most affected by the policies 
being developed. She also emphasized the importance of centering people who are most affected by the 
policies being developed. 
o Councilor Grant reiterated that homelessness itself is not a crime and that police cannot solve the 
housing crisis. Refer to the video. 
o Andre Clark encouraged the committee to consider the impacts of Burlington Forward based on income 
and housing status. He shared observations regarding enforcement activity involving people 
experiencing homelessness and expressed concern about arrests and enforcement being used in 
situations where alternative approaches may be possible. He encouraged committee members to hear 
directly from people who use drugs, people experiencing homelessness, people in recovery, and mutual 
aid organizations. Refer to the video. 
o Councilor Grant provided additional context regarding low-level offenses, the State’s criminal justice 
framework, and the Accountability Court.  
• Adjournment 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson adjourned the meeting at 7:13 pm
